items.headline: Add inline captions, cross-references, and tables of captions in Google Docs
items.summary: Google Docs makes it easy to create, structure, and collaborate on complex documents across formats, including viewing and editing Microsoft Word (.docx) files directly in Docs. Today, we are introducing three new Google Docs features— inline captions , cross-references , and tables of captions —to help you more easily organize, reference, and navigate figures, tables, equations, and other items in your documents. Inline captions: Insert numbered labels (such as “Figure 1” or “Table 1”, or define your own custom labels) that automatically order and renumber themselves in sequence as captions are added, reordered, or removed. Cross-references: Link directly to existing captions in your docume
lines: Google Docs adds three features: inline captions, cross-references, and tables of captions.
Inline captions insert numbered labels, such as Figure 1 or Table 1, or custom labels, that renumber automatically as captions are added, reordered, or removed.
Cross-references link directly to existing captions, helping users organize and navigate figures, tables, equations, and other items.
For business users, these features help structure and reference complex documents, including .docx files viewed and edited in Docs.

lines: Gemini Notebook can now turn sources into interactive sites that help users make sense of complex information.
Users type 'make me a site' in the Gemini Notebook chat with a description, then open the result in a new tab or share it.
Examples include interactive periodic tables, historical timelines, quarterly sales dashboards, and project management trackers.
For business users, this offers a way to turn notes and research into dashboards and task trackers.

items.headline: Amazon OpenSearch Memory is now generally available
items.summary: Today, AWS announced the general availability of Amazon OpenSearch Memory, a new serverless capability in Amazon OpenSearch Service for adding persistent memory to AI agents. OpenSearch Memory stores agent interactions as searchable events, derives useful memories, and retrieves relevant context across sessions, so agents can recall prior decisions, earlier interactions, and user preferences without replaying the full conversation history to the model. Customers can give agents long-term memory without provisioning infrastructure or building separate extraction, indexing, consolidation, and retrieval systems. OpenSearch Memory stores the original events verbatim, makes them searchable within
lines: AWS announced general availability of Amazon OpenSearch Memory, a serverless capability in Amazon OpenSearch Service for adding persistent memory to AI agents.
It stores agent interactions as searchable events, derives memories, and retrieves relevant context across sessions.
Customers can add long-term agent memory without provisioning infrastructure or building separate extraction, indexing, consolidation, and retrieval systems.

items.headline: Introducing the Apache Spark Optimization Agent for AWS Glue ETL
items.summary: AWS Glue ETL now offers the Apache Spark Optimization Agent, which analyzes completed Spark job runs and delivers cost and performance optimization recommendations within minutes. You can select a cost or performance goal, and the agent returns specific configuration changes with the telemetry evidence and reasoning behind each suggestion. You can use the agent on any completed job run from the AWS Glue console, or from your own tools through the Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio MCP Server. The agent takes the job's configuration, logs, and Spark telemetry together with your chosen goal and returns recommendations computed by a deterministic recommendation engine. The engine reads all job art
lines: AWS Glue ETL now offers the Apache Spark Optimization Agent, which analyzes completed Spark job runs and recommends cost or performance changes.
Users select a cost or performance goal, and the agent returns configuration changes with supporting telemetry and reasoning.
The agent can run from the AWS Glue console or through the Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio MCP Server.
For data teams, this offers a way to review Spark job tuning based on configuration, logs, and telemetry.

items.headline: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports cross-Region inference routing
items.summary: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces cross-Region inference routing, which helps keep inference applications available when a region runs short of capacity by sending requests to endpoints deployed in other AWS Regions and AWS accounts. Models served on accelerated instances can reach capacity limits in a single Region, and an unhealthy endpoint can lead to throttling and errors for end users. Previously, teams had to build and maintain their own routing, health checks, and retry logic across Regions. With cross-Region inference routing in SageMaker AI, developers create an inference router, register the real-time endpoints, asynchronous endpoints, and inference components they already run,
lines: Amazon SageMaker AI announced cross-Region inference routing, which sends requests to endpoints in other AWS Regions and accounts when a Region runs short of capacity.
Developers create an inference router and register the real-time endpoints, asynchronous endpoints, and inference components they already run.
The feature aims to keep inference applications available when capacity limits or unhealthy endpoints would otherwise cause throttling and errors for end users.

items.headline: AWS announces ExtendDB 1.0
items.summary: Today, Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced version 1.0 of ExtendDB, the first release of the open source Amazon DynamoDB-compatible adapter for production use. ExtendDB is fully compatible with the DynamoDB API and runs on a database backend that you choose, so developers and infrastructure teams can run DynamoDB workloads in on-premises data centers, in private or public clouds, and at the edge without rewriting application code. ExtendDB 1.0 supports four storage backends, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cassandra, and MongoDB. For local development and continuous integration (CI), the extenddb-dev container image and the @extenddb/dev npm package run a DynamoDB-compatible endpoint over SQLite, so you
lines: AWS announced version 1.0 of ExtendDB, an open source Amazon DynamoDB-compatible adapter, as its first release for production use.
ExtendDB is fully compatible with the DynamoDB API and runs on a database backend the user chooses.
Version 1.0 supports PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cassandra, and MongoDB as storage backends.
Teams can run DynamoDB workloads on-premises, in private or public clouds, and at the edge without rewriting application code.

items.headline: AWS Transform custom now supports cross-account sharing of transformation definitions
items.summary: AWS Transform custom now enables you to share transformation definitions (TDs) and their associated lessons across AWS accounts, organizational units (OUs), or your entire organization in AWS Organizations through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). AWS Transform custom is a capability of AWS Transform that performs transformations across your technology stack, including API and framework upgrades, migrations, and language translations. With this launch, you can share TDs as live resources rather than static copies, so consumers run the owner's latest published version by default while the owner maintains full control. As the TD owner, you select from four managed permissions ranging from
lines: AWS Transform custom now supports sharing transformation definitions and their lessons across AWS accounts, organizational units, or an AWS Organization through AWS RAM.
Shared definitions are live resources, so consumers run the owner's latest published version by default.
Owners choose from four managed permissions and keep full control of their definitions.
For IT teams, this supports standardizing transformations across accounts while the owner retains control.

items.headline: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
items.summary: A flaw in NGINX's HTTP/2 support can allow an attacker to run code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled, without needing to log in. The decade-old flaw, CVE-2026-123007, dubbed "nginx2root," has been present in NGINX's open-source code since version 1.9.5, released on September 22, 2015. Fixed versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 came out today. F5, the company behind NGINX, says attackers can run code where
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: A flaw in NGINX's HTTP/2 support can let an attacker run code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled, without logging in.
The flaw, CVE-2026-123007 and dubbed 'nginx2root,' has been in NGINX open-source code since version 1.9.5, released September 22, 2015.
Fixed versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 have been released.
IT teams running NGINX with HTTP/2 enabled should check their versions against the fixed releases.

"These releases are part of PHP's regular four-week release cycle and will address security vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions," the maintainers said.
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: The PHP maintainers issued an advisory announcing an upcoming security release that addresses critical flaws.
The release is scheduled for November 19, 2026, between 2 and 2:30 p.m. UTC.

items.headline: Ruby Releases Fixes for 7 Regex and String Flaws, Warns 5 Have Proof-of-Concept RCE
items.summary: Ruby contains seven memory-safety flaws in its regular expression engine and its string case-conversion code. For five of them, its maintainers say, proof-of-concept exploits, or PoCs, have shown that crafted input can run code on the machine. "We are aware of PoCs that prove some of them can be used to trigger remote code execution," the maintainers said. The project released fixed versions
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Ruby released fixes for seven flaws in its regular expression engine and string case-conversion code, which contain memory-safety issues.
For five of the flaws, proof-of-concept exploits have shown that crafted input can run code on the machine, according to the maintainers.
Teams running Ruby should apply the fixed versions released by the project, since some of the flaws may be used for remote code execution.

items.headline: Researcher Demonstrates Database RCE Exploits Affecting PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
items.summary: Low-privilege database accounts that cannot read a single application table can still be used to run code on the database server itself, a researcher has shown, by reaching memory-corruption bugs in the engine code behind ordinary SQL. The exploits, published yesterday, are the researcher's proofs of concept against PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus a separate Oracle chain that needs no
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: A researcher demonstrated that low-privilege database accounts that cannot read any application table can still run code on the database server by reaching memory-corruption bugs in the engine code behind ordinary SQL.
The published proofs of concept target PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, and a separate Oracle chain that needs no further details in the text.
Database accounts with limited privileges may not be enough to contain risk, so administrators may want to review database security controls.

items.headline: Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions
items.summary: Today, the Reserve Bank released the second edition of its biennial Report titled “ Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions ”. The theme of this edition is ‘Local Finances and Capacity Building in Rural India’. Drawing upon a balanced panel of 2.25 lakh Gram Panchayats for the period 2022-23 to 2024-25, the Report presents an assessment of their finances and their role in achieving sustainable and inclusive rural socio-economic development. Highlights: Gram Panchayat finances strengthened during 2022-23 and 2023-24; they, however, remain dependent on intergovernmental transfers, accounting for about 90 per cent of total receipts, while own source revenues (OSR) accounted for a modest share o
lines: The Reserve Bank of India released the second edition of its biennial report, 'Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions,' themed 'Local Finances and Capacity Building in Rural India.'
The report uses a balanced panel of 2.25 lakh Gram Panchayats for 2022-23 to 2024-25.
Gram Panchayat finances strengthened in 2022-23 and 2023-24, but about 90 per cent of total receipts came from intergovernmental transfers, with own source revenues a modest share.
Finance and policy teams tracking rural local government budgets can use the report's assessment of revenue dependence.

source.name: Reserve Bank of India press releases

items.headline: Sending From Email Aliases – General Availability
items.summary: Today we are announcing the General Availability (GA) of Sending from Aliases for Exchange Online. This was a highly requested feature that now empowers users to send emails from any alias (proxy address) associated with their mailbox, not just their primary SMTP address. Read on to learn how it works, how to enable it, and what’s next. What Is Sending From Aliases? Sending from Aliases allows Exchange Online users to send emails using any of their configured aliases or proxy (or secondary) SMTP addresses. Previously, aliases could only receive mail, and all outgoing messages used the primary SMTP address of the mailbox. Workarounds like shared mailboxes or distribution groups were used in t
lines: Exchange Online now has General Availability of Sending from Aliases, which lets users send email from any alias (proxy address) on their mailbox, not just the primary SMTP address.
Previously, aliases could only receive mail, and outgoing messages used the primary SMTP address.
For IT teams, this can reduce reliance on workarounds such as shared mailboxes or distribution groups when users need to send from an alias.

items.headline: Improved syncing of guest additions across calendar services
items.summary: We are introducing key interoperability enhancements in Google Calendar to improve how guest additions are handled across calendar platforms. When a Google Calendar guest adds new guests to an event organized on a third-party calendar service, such as Microsoft Outlook, Google Calendar now automatically notifies the organizer via email. Conversely, when Google Calendar receives a similar notification from a third-party calendar service, it now automatically updates the event with the newly added guests. This improves the synchronization of guest lists across platforms and ensures that newly added guests seamlessly receive any subsequent event updates made by the organizer. Getting started Ad
lines: Google Calendar now automatically emails the organizer when a Google Calendar guest adds guests to an event organized on a third-party calendar service, such as Microsoft Outlook.
When a third-party calendar service sends a similar notification, Google Calendar now updates the event with the newly added guests.
The change keeps guest lists in sync across calendar platforms, so new guests receive later event updates from the organizer.

This will help keep meetings focused and interactive, with less disruptions caused by sending links in chat and managing permissions from other apps while trying to present. items.headline: PHP Fixes 7 Critical Flaws, Including Bugs That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
items.summary: The PHP Foundation has released security updates to address multiple critical security flaws that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution on affected deployments, including CVE-2026-115560. The release of the patch follows an advance notice in which the project maintainers alerted users to multiple critical vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions under specific
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: The PHP Foundation released security updates for multiple critical flaws that could be exploited for remote code execution on affected deployments.
The release includes CVE-2026-115560 and follows an advance notice from project maintainers about the vulnerabilities.
IT teams running PHP deployments should check their versions and apply the security updates.

items.headline: PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs
items.summary: The PHP development team released security updates addressing 18 vulnerabilities, including critical flaws that could allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on vulnerable servers. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: The PHP development team released security updates fixing 18 vulnerabilities, including critical flaws that could let unauthenticated attackers execute code remotely on vulnerable servers.
Administrators running PHP on servers should confirm whether their versions include the fixes.

items.headline: Critical VMware vCenter Flaw (CVSS 9.8) Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
items.summary: A critical flaw in VMware vCenter lets an attacker with network access bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system, Broadcom, which owns VMware, said in an advisory published today. Fixed versions are out for all supported branches, and the company lists no workaround. vCenter is the central console for managing an organization's ESX hosts and virtual machines. The
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: A critical VMware vCenter flaw, rated CVSS 9.8, lets network attackers bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access, according to a Broadcom advisory.
Fixed versions are available for all supported branches, and the company lists no workaround.
vCenter is the central console for managing an organization's ESX hosts and virtual machines, so admins should apply the fixed versions.

items.headline: JPMorgan Chase reveals data breach, but says it’s unrelated to this week’s banking outage
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase says its third-party vendors suffered a cyberattack, exposing marketing data like customer names and email addresses. The confirmation follows a report from Cybernews, which says a ransomware group leaked email addresses belonging to around 16,000 JPMorgan Chase customers. In a post about the attack, JPMorgan Chase says "there is no connection" to the […]
lines: Reported by The Verge: JPMorgan Chase says its third-party vendors suffered a cyberattack that exposed marketing data, such as customer names and email addresses.
Cybernews reported that a ransomware group leaked email addresses belonging to around 16,000 JPMorgan Chase customers.
JPMorgan Chase states there is no connection between the data breach and this week's banking outage.
The incident highlights the need for IT teams to review third-party access to customer contact data.

items.headline: Amazon UK drops the prices of the new Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max for Prime subscribers
items.summary: No, it’s not Prime Day – but Amazon UK still has an interesting Prime-only deal. The Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max started their global rollout just a couple of days ago and the retailer is already offering discounts of £100 and £150, respectively. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max and Xiaomi 18 Pro The catch is that you need an active Prime subscription to get this deal. You can use the free 30-day trial for that. If you already used it for Prime Day, you can just subscribe – Prime costs £8.99 a month or £95 for a full year, so it will pay for itself with these discounts. ...
lines: Reported by GSMArena news: Amazon UK is offering discounts of £100 on the Xiaomi 18 Pro and £150 on the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max for Prime subscribers.
An active Prime subscription is required, and the free 30-day trial can be used; Prime costs £8.99 a month or £95 for a full year.
The offer applies to individual buyers who hold a Prime membership.

items.headline: UK government forced to disclose secret Apple backdoor order
items.summary: The U.K. tribunal's ruling rejected London's claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.
lines: Reported by TechCrunch: A U.K. tribunal ruled that the government must disclose a secret order related to an Apple backdoor.
The tribunal rejected London's claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.
The ruling gives public visibility into a government demand affecting Apple products, which may interest IT teams tracking such requests.

items.headline: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
items.summary: Ransomware attacks often involve credential theft, lateral movement, and attempts to disable security controls long before encryption begins. Acronis examines five warning signs that can help defenders detect intrusions earlier, contain malicious activity, and protect critical systems and backups. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: Acronis outlines five warning signs that can help defenders detect ransomware intrusions before encryption or data theft.
Ransomware attacks often involve credential theft, lateral movement, and attempts to disable security controls before encryption begins.
Monitoring for these early signs can help IT teams contain malicious activity and protect critical systems and backups.

items.headline: Critical NGINX ‘NGINX2Root’ bugs let attackers hijack servers
items.summary: Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities dubbed "nginx2root" allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers, with researchers demonstrating how the flaws can be chained with a Linux kernel bug to gain root access. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities, dubbed nginx2root, allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers.
Researchers demonstrated chaining the flaws with a Linux kernel bug to gain root access.
Administrators running NGINX web servers should review their deployments for exposure to these flaws.
